s1.syndrome_frame: Acute respiratory failure with mediastinal mass and multiple organ involvement
salient_findings: Dyspnea on exertion and intermittent dry cough
Acute worsening of dyspnea leading to respiratory failure
Mediastinal mass compressing and displacing the trachea
Pleural component with mass effect on surrounding structures
Lytic destruction of vertebrae and pneumomediastinum
key_facts: 1-month history of dyspnea on exertion and intermittent dry cough
Hyporexia and unquantified intermittent fever
Delayed care until acute worsening of dyspnea
Developed acute respiratory failure and pulseless electrical activity arrest
Required orotracheal intubation and stabilization
Blood pressure 200/140 mmHg, heart rate 100 bpm, respiratory rate 16 bpm
Oxygen saturation 78% on ventilatory support
Anisocoria, jugular venous distension, sinus tachycardia, and bilateral coarse rales
Homogeneous right paratracheal mediastinal mass on chest radiography
Lobulated solid mass arising from the right thoracic operculum/pleura on CT scan
Nodular pleural component, mass effect on surrounding structures, and lytic destruction of vertebrae
WBC 13.47 × 10^3/µL, hemoglobin 9.9 g/dL, platelets 303 × 10^3/µL
Elevated lactic acid, C-reactive protein, and LDH

shortlist.label: Hodgkin lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Mediastinal mass and lymphadenopathy are common in Hodgkin lymphoma

shortlist.label: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive lymphoma can cause rapid progression of symptoms and mediastinal involvement

shortlist.label: Thymoma
shortlist.why_kept: Thymoma can cause mediastinal mass and respiratory symptoms

shortlist.label: Thymic carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Thymic carcinoma is a rare but aggressive tumor that can cause mediastinal mass and respiratory failure

shortlist.label: Primary mediastinal large B-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: This lymphoma subtype often presents with a large mediastinal mass and can cause respiratory symptoms
